paragraphs.source_en: The master, realizing that in an exchange of abuse he was no match for Nose, was forced to remain silent for a while. Then, as if something had suddenly occurred to him, he said, “You keep saying that Kangetsu is in love with your daughter, but what I heard is a little different. Come now, Meitei, isn’t that so?” The master appealed to Meitei for rescue. Meitei said, “Well, according to what Kangetsu said at the time, it was your daughter who first fell ill. I seem to recall he said she had been delirious.” “There is absolutely no such thing.” Mrs. Kaneda spoke in a perfectly clear, direct, straight-line manner. Meitei said, “Even so, Kangetsu certainly said he had heard it from the wife of a certain doctor.” Nose said, “That was a trick of mine. I deliberately asked the doctor’s wife to sound out Mr. Kangetsu for me.” The master said, “And this certain lady understood your purpose and agreed to it?” “Yes. Of course I could hardly ask her for nothing. I sent her all sorts of things.” Meitei said, “So you have made up your mind to dig into every last detail about Kangetsu, and not go home until you have it all clear?” Meitei, too, seemed somewhat displeased, and used a harsh tone he seldom employed. Then he said to the master, “Well then, Kushami, it costs us nothing to tell her. Let us tell her. Madam, both I and Kushami can tell you anything about Kangetsu, provided it is fact and causes him no difficulty. Yes, it would be best if you asked in order, one item at a time.”

paragraphs.source_en: Nose seemed satisfied and began to put forward her questions. And the rough tone she had just used toward Meitei changed back into politeness. “I hear Mr. Kangetsu is also a Bachelor of Science. What, after all, is his specialty?” The master answered solemnly, “At graduate school he is researching the earth’s magnetism.” Unfortunately Nose did not understand what the master meant, so she said, “Heh!” and, with a puzzled look on her face, asked, “If he studies that, can he become a doctor?” The master asked unhappily, “Do you mean that if he cannot become a doctor, you will not give him your daughter?” “Yes. Mere bachelors of science are everywhere.” Nose answered without the least concern. The master looked at Meitei, his expression growing still more disgusted. Meitei, also not in very good humor, said, “Whether he becomes a doctor or not is not something we can guarantee, so please ask about something else.” Nose said, “Even lately, is he still studying that earth... whatever it is?” The master answered without thinking, “Only two or three days ago he delivered a lecture at the Physical Society on the results of a study called the mechanics of hanging.” Nose said, “Oh, how dreadful! Hanging, of all things. He really is an eccentric! If he studies things like hanging, I doubt he can possibly become a doctor.” The master replied, “If he hangs himself, then of course becoming a doctor would be difficult. But if it is the mechanics of hanging, it is not necessarily impossible.” Nose watched the master’s expression and said, “Is that so?” Sadly, Nose did not know what mechanics meant, and so she remained uneasy inside. On the other hand, she probably felt that asking the master to explain such a thing would touch her dignity, so she could only judge whether he was telling the truth by reading his face. The master’s face looked sour. Nose asked again, “Besides that, does he study anything a little easier to understand?” The master answered, “Let me see. The other day he wrote a paper entitled ‘On the Stability of Acorns, with Reference to the Movements of the Heavenly Bodies.’” Nose asked, “Do they study things like acorns at the university too?” Meitei took up the thread from the side and, teasing her deliberately, said, “Well, I am a layman myself, so I do not really know. At any rate, since Kangetsu is working on it, I suppose it must have some value as research.” Nose seemed to feel that questions about scholarship were too much for her, and so she gave up pursuing them. Changing the subject, she asked, “I would like to ask about something else. Is it true that this New Year he broke two front teeth eating shiitake mushrooms?” Meitei, deciding that answering this sort of question was just his specialty, immediately came to life and said, “Indeed. In the place where those teeth broke, there was even a bit of Kuya mochi stuck.” Nose said, “What an utterly careless man he is. Why does he not pick it out with a toothpick?” “The next time I see him, I shall remind him.” The master said this with a chuckle.
